summary: Revise at 5.6. The plant now reads: a jeweller who sees the 300 px hero and face says 'wild rose with a hip' from the pinnate toothed leaves, the thorny canes and the red fruit. As a Kings of Alchemy piece it is still a thin wire bramble band with a caged bead, well below Caiman's 7 and the Reptilia sheet. Five of the eight checklist items fail. (1) Density: about 85% of the ring is two bare 1.4 mm canes carrying 10 small prickles, and all the ornament sits in a 70-degree arc at the crown. Caiman is worked across the whole visible surface. (2) The calyx is still the cage read-test 5 warned about: five wire spokes run over the stone to a central boss. In face.png it reads as a ship's wheel or a four-claw cage, not sepals. (3) The leaflets are flat extruded plates with a coned midrib, vertical side walls and stair-stepped teeth (leaf-close.png, stones.png). Every rachis ends in a blunt sawn cylinder butted into its terminal leaflet. That is mechanical CAD, not sculpted form. (4) The hip is a 5.6 round cabochon, though the rethink specifies an orange-red oval 6.4 x 4.8. It renders at transmission 0.72 with visible facet banding, and stones.json still labels it 'Ruby, Round 4.0'. (5) Several palm prickles end in flat-capped cylindrical stubs (palm.png, reverse.png). Gates: the mesh, notes, DFM, stone count, cold reload, export and template gates are green. The lost-wax wall gate is not green as the review rule states it. It judges leaflet blades (0.36-0.53 mm) and sepals (0.25 mm) at the 0.15 mm pointed-detail floor. Those are plate walls, not points, and the Manticora precedent covered only a tapering aculeus tip. That alone is an automatic revise. Two rounds remain, which is enough for a concrete fix, but reaching 7.5 needs a real gain in mass and density, not polish.
strengths: The plant reads at 300 px without a caption: pinnate five-leaflet toothed leaves, a prickled cane and a red hip together say dog rose or briar. Read-test 5 passed, and the face view confirms it.
The silhouette is distinct inside Vepres: an open two-cane twine with an off-axis crown spray. No signet or band among the other rings looks like it.
One theme from face to palm: canes and prickles run all the way round, and nothing foreign is scattered on the ring.
The canes are honest closed, tapered twisted sweeps with a real over-under crossing at the shoulders (bare-vs-finished.png). The twist shows in the highlights.
The engineering is clean: one shell, watertight, 0 degenerates and 0 crossings on all 28 made parts, 0 DFM findings, cold reload identical, a 279 KB template with 1 patch.
The hook direction of the prickles is varied, and the prickles that render well (hero lower left) have a convincing hooked rose-thorn profile.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Briar cane, prickles, rose leaves and hip only. The palm thins to cane and prickles, which suits a briar. Nothing foreign appears.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and face-300 read as wild rose with hip (read-test 5 agrees). The read is marginal: the calyx cage and the coin-like leaflets could tip it to 'caged bead on laurel'.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: Leaflet teeth show stair-stepped, saw-cut side walls in leaf-close.png and stones.png (the lower-right leaflets especially). The leaflet faces are coned plates with radial shading streaks. The rachis-to-terminal-leaflet joins are blunt cylinder butts (face.png left and right).

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as the plant's fruit
checklist.reason: It sits in a made bezel on a receptacle, and the orange-red colour is right. But the calyx spokes cross the stone's face to a central boss and cage it, and about 30% of the dome is covered. It is round 5.6, not the specified oval 6.4 x 4.8 hip. It renders translucent (transmission 0.72) for an 'opaque' hip, with visible tessellation bands on the dome. stones.json mislabels it 'Ruby, Round 4.0' with reference-ruby.stl.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The leaflets are constant-thickness extrusions with vertical walls. The rachis is a uniform tube ending in a flat-cut butt. Palm prickles at about theta 200, 240, 330 and 20 end in flat disc caps (palm.png, reverse.png). The receptacle underside shows a flat disc (palm.png).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable: CAD-only, with no factory stock.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: An open twin-cane twine with an asymmetric crown spray. No other Vepres ring is built yet, and none is planned like it.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large form (the hip, 5.6) and small forms (prickles, teeth) are present, but the medium layer is missing along about 290 degrees of the ring: there is no bark, no leaf nodes, no stipules, no side shoots. There are only 10 prickles on about 140 mm of cane. Each cane is a 1.4 mm wire, so the ring weighs 4.7 g of 18k and looks sparse against Caiman's fully worked surface.

punch_list.zone: Rose leaf 1 and 2, all 10 leaflets; hip calyx sepals 1-5
punch_list.change: Make leaflet blades and sepals pass the 0.8 mm lost-wax wall. Thicken each leaflet to a 0.8 mm minimum at the midrib, tapering to no less than 0.5 mm only within 0.4 mm of the toothed edge. Report that edge band separately as a 'blade edge' detail class with its own named floor, and get Logan's sign-off on it. Give sepals a 0.8 mm root section, tapering to a point only over the last 1.0 mm. Report each sepal's root and tip separately. Resample Rose leaf 2 with fewer than 1000 skipped hard-edge faces.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json ray_walls shows every leaflet and sepal body at sampled_min_mm >= 0.8 (or >= 0.5 at a declared blade edge that Logan signed off on). The gate line names the detail classes explicitly. No part skips more than 1000 hard-edge faces.

punch_list.change: Remove the cage. Delete the five spokes that cross the dome and the central boss as it stands. Grow five sepals from a 1.6 mm boss at the hip's distal tip only. Each sepal is 0.8 mm at the root, 2.2-2.6 mm long, and curls back down over the dome so that none crosses more than 20% of the stone's radius inward from the rim. Two sepals carry 2-3 pinnate side lobes. Hold the stone with a plain bezel lip from the receptacle, not with the sepals.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-300 the hip shows as an unbroken red dome over at least 85% of its face, with a small gold star at one end. In face.png no gold line runs from rim to centre, and nothing reads as prongs or a wheel.

punch_list.change: Change the hip to the specified oval cabochon 6.4 x 4.8, long axis along the finger. Make it opaque: transmission no more than 0.1, roughness about 0.25, tint about [0.72, 0.20, 0.06]. Raise stone tessellation so the dome has no visible facet bands. Regenerate stones.json from the design.
punch_list.acceptance: stones.png shows a smooth, opaque oval hip with no banding. stones.json names the 6.4 x 4.8 oval cabochon and agrees with report.json.

punch_list.change: Sculpt the leaflets. Make each a pointed oval about 3.2 x 2.0 mm with a domed upper face (0.25 mm sag across the width) and a sunk midvein. Taper the thickness toward the edge, with no vertical extrusion wall over 0.3 mm tall. Make the teeth 0.15-0.2 mm, forward-hooked and fading toward the base, cut from a smooth outline sampled at no less than 0.05 mm, so there are no stair-steps. Tilt each leaflet pair 15-20 degrees off the rachis. Blend each rachis into its terminal leaflet over at least 1.0 mm, with no flat butt.
punch_list.acceptance: In leaf-close.png every leaflet shows a curved face catching a graded highlight and a continuous edge with no stepped walls. The rachis flows into the terminal leaflet without a visible cut circle. In face-300 the leaflets read as pointed ovals, not coins.

punch_list.zone: Both canes, full 360 degrees, weighted to theta 0-60 and 120-360 (shoulders and palm)
punch_list.change: Add the missing medium layer and raise density to Caiman's. Swell each cane to 1.8 mm at the crown, tapering to 1.4 at the palm. Raise the prickles from 10 to at least 28: 8 per shoulder and 6 per palm quarter, crown ones 1.4x the palm ones, each a flattened triangular base about 0.8 x 1.0 mm hooked back. Add 4 leaf nodes per cane with stipule collars, plus 2 short cut side shoots, 1.2 mm across, at the shoulders (about theta 30 and 150). Add bark: shallow longitudinal fissures 0.1 mm deep, kept to the side faces.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero-300 every 45-degree sector of visible cane shows at least one prickle or node, and the canes no longer read as plain wire. Side-by-side with caiman/hero.png at equal size, the ornamented share of the visible surface is comparable.

punch_list.zone: Palm prickles, about theta 200, 240, 330 and 20; receptacle underside
punch_list.change: Re-aim or re-cap the prickles that render as flat-capped cylinders so every prickle ends in a hooked point. Most likely the twist path is clipped or the view is end-on: give each tip end_scale no more than 0.4 and a visible hook. Round the flat disc on the receptacle's underside into a sculpted receptacle base, a 0.6 mm fillet into the stalk.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png and reverse.png show no flat disc ends on any prickle and no flat circular face on the receptacle underside.

punch_list.zone: Cane forks at the face-view flanks, about theta 40-55 and 125-140
punch_list.change: Blend the bulbous, beaked fork lumps into a smooth parting, trimming about 1 mm, and carry the leaf petioles into the cane with a 0.3 mm seam bead.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-300 neither end of the crown shows a bud- or beak-shaped lump, and each petiole meets its cane without a visible step.
